findings.problem: The proof re-derives, twice by hand (outer: `rw [grading_piece_eq_iSup] at hz` + `iSup_le`/`map₂_le` + `comap`; inner: `grading_piece_eq_iSup` + `iSup_le`/`map₂_le` + `comap`), the principle 'a linear map out of a balanced tensor product is homogeneous if it is on homogeneous pure tensors'. That principle is already a library lemma, `BalancedTensorProduct.map_mem_of_tmul` / `isHomogeneous_of_tmul`, in Grading/Basic.lean. The proof also repeats the degree bookkeeping (`omega` for r + (q - r + (p - q)) = p, plus `simpa only [hdegree]`), which the helper absorbs. The two layers of `mem_comap`/`mk_apply`/`LinearEquiv.coe_coe` unfolding obscure that the argument is just 'check on pure tensors twice'. The sibling proof `assocCarrier_mem` in GradedModuleCat/BimoduleTensor/Associator.lean uses exactly the helper twice.
findings.proposed_change: Drop the manual iSup/map₂ blocks and use the helper at both stages. Outer stage: `isHomogeneous_of_tmul (𝒜 := 𝒞) (grading (𝒜 := ℬ) G H) I (GR).piece assoc.toLinearMap 0 (fun {p q x y} hx hy => ?_)`. In the remaining goal, `assoc (tmul x y) ∈ (GR).piece (p + q + 0)`, apply `map_mem_of_tmul (𝒜 := ℬ) G H (GR).piece f q ?_ hx`, with `f := assoc.toLinearMap ∘ₗ (mk R C).flip y` as now. The inner hypothesis, for m ∈ G.piece a and n ∈ H.piece b, is `assoc (tmul (tmul m n) y) = tmul m (tmul n y) ∈ (GR).piece (a + b + q)`. It follows from `tmul_mem_grading (𝒜 := ℬ) G (grading (𝒜 := 𝒞) H I) hm (tmul_mem_grading (𝒜 := 𝒞) H I hn hy)` after rewriting with `add_assoc`. Finish with `simpa only [add_zero]`. No `omega` or `grading_piece_eq_iSup` is needed in this file.
findings.benefit: The proof shrinks to two helper calls and one `tmul_mem_grading` composition, so the mathematical content (associativity of degree addition) is visible. It no longer depends on the internal `iSup`/`map₂` description of pieces, so a change to `grading_piece_eq_iSup` would not break it. It also matches how the same two-stage argument is already written for graded bimodules, which removes a divergent copy of the machinery.
